title: Count of good Index inputs
statement: Let $n$ be a positive integer and let $p$ be a deterministic one-way protocol for the Index problem on $n$-bit inputs. The number of inputs that lie at Hamming distance less than $n/4$ from some answer vector of $p$ is at most $|A|\,2\binom{n}{\lfloor n/4\rfloor}$, where $A$ is the set of answer vectors of $p$.
hypotheses_covered: $p$ is a deterministic one-way protocol from $n$-bit Boolean inputs and indices in $[n]$ to Boolean outputs
replaced:
Let $\mathrm{good}$ be the set of inputs $x \in \{0,1\}^n$ that are not bad for $p$ (those
within Hamming distance $< n/4$ of some answer vector).  Then
\[
  \abs{\mathrm{good}} \le \abs{A} \cdot 2 \binom{n}{\lfloor n/4 \rfloor},
\]
where $A$ is the answer set of $p$.
